a1
Sarah died at Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in Canaan. She was one hundred twenty-seven years old.
a2
Abraham came to mourn for her, and to weep.
b1
Then he stood before the Hittites: I am a stranger and a guest among you. Give me a burial place of my own.
b2
They answered: you are a prince among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs.
c1
Abraham bowed, and asked for the cave of Machpelah, at the edge of Ephron's field.
c2
Ephron said: take the field and the cave. I give them to you.
c3
But Abraham insisted on paying the full price.
d1
Ephron said: four hundred shekels of silver. What is that between us? Bury your dead.
d2
Abraham weighed out the silver, in front of everyone at the city gate.
e1
The field, the cave, and its trees became Abraham's.
e2
There he buried Sarah his wife, facing Mamre.
h1
Abraham was a stranger in the land God had promised, mourning his wife.
h2
He wept, and then he rose and did what love asked.
h3
Grief and faith stand together. Tears are not a lack of trust.
h4
Today, honor someone you miss with one loving act.
i
How do you honor the people you miss?
